name: FL-23
label: Safe D

model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district leans Democratic by about nine points, incumbent Lois Frankel has outraised Deborah Adeimy by more than ten to one, outside groups have spent only on Frankel's behalf, and betting markets put her odds near 96-97%. With no public polling and no expert ratings flagging the race, the fundamentals-driven estimate of a roughly 20-point Democratic margin stands.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Frankel or a sharp shift in the national political environment could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel, a Democratic incumbent seeking another term in this South Florida district, faces Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy. The seat leans Democratic by about nine points, and Frankel has built a dominant financial position, raising roughly $2.3 million with $1.2 million still on hand. Adeimy has raised about $162,000, and outside groups have spent modestly to support Frankel and nothing against her.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, candidate finances, and betting markets, which put Frankel's chances at 96 to 97 percent. Incumbency, a favorable national environment, and the challenger's limited resources all point toward a comfortable Democratic win, with the main caveat being the absence of polling to confirm the fundamentals.
